correctness.rationale: The private pendant prohibits omitting both members of any base/leaf pair. For omitted cores A and omitted leaves B, super domination holds iff no A-B base edge exists. For an empty pair, adding its core works exactly when it sees no B; adding its leaf works exactly when it sees no A. Monotonicity of super domination under selecting more vertices turns these singleton obstructions into an exact maximality condition. In a cyclic base every empty pair separates alternating nonempty A and B runs, so the number of separators is 2j and the positive-run composition count proves the displayed coefficient. Literal direct subset enumeration and independent checks of the exact expressions passed over the stated finite ranges; they corroborate rather than prove the infinite case.

value.rationale: An October 2026 full all-set pendant-corona polynomial reveals a natural unresolved structural refinement: which sets are inclusion-minimal and how many exist at each size. The new general A/B/E criterion solves this for every one-leaf corona, while the sunlet consequence determines an infinite-family inclusion-minimal polynomial, all possible sizes, a sharp four-period upper parameter and exact maximum-set multiplicities. The parity-spaced upper spectrum is a substantial natural graph invariant, distinct from known minimum counts and the all-set polynomial.
